name: Legal chess
purpose: Play chess against an app that never accepts or plays an illegal move. Every move goes to the verified holo in your browser; it checks your move against the legal moves of the position, plays it, and answers with its own reply. It looks two moves ahead, so it is a modest opponent.
placeholder: 70-character position, a space, a move such as e2e4
outputLabel: Position after the reply, the reply, the status

promise.headline: Never plays or accepts an illegal move.
promise.detail: Every move, yours and the app's, is checked against the rules of movement and king safety before it is played.

claim: LC-01 and LC-02: the app plays a reply, and accepts a move of yours, only when the legality gate returns Legal for that exact move. LC-03: the legal moves the gate checks against reproduce the published perft counts of five reference positions to depth three.

proposition.name: playsOnlyLegal
proposition.text:
playsOnlyLegal check answer :=
  match answer with
  | Played _ => isLegal check
  | Passed   => true

reply pos := gate (candidate pos) (verdict pos (candidate pos))

verdict pos move :=
  if isLegalMove pos move then Legal else Illegal
proposition.plain: If the app plays a move, the verdict on that move, computed by isLegalMove from the rules of movement and king safety, is Legal. Your moves pass through the same verdict before they are played.

theorems.name: gate_plays_only_legal
theorems.statement: playsOnlyLegal check (gate choice check) = true, for every move and every verdict
theorems.how: Proved by cases on the verdict, checked by the Lean kernel and leanchecker in prismpm verify, with no axiom

theorems.name: reply_is_legal
theorems.statement: playsOnlyLegal (verdict pos (candidate pos)) (reply pos) = true, for every position
theorems.how: Proved by applying gate_plays_only_legal to the engine's candidate and its verdict

theorems.name: gate_accepts_only_legal
theorems.statement: acceptsOnlyLegal check (admitGate pos move check) = true, for every position, move and verdict
theorems.how: Proved by cases on the verdict, checked by the Lean kernel and leanchecker in prismpm verify

theorems.name: admit_is_legal
theorems.statement: acceptsOnlyLegal (verdict pos move) (admitMove pos move) = true, for every position and move
theorems.how: Proved by applying gate_accepts_only_legal to the move's own verdict

pinned.name: chess_lc_01, chess_lc_02
pinned.what: The theorems' exact statements, that the verdict is isLegalMove, that every reply the app returns comes from reply and every visitor move goes through admitMove, and that nothing plays a move around the gate. String-matching tests, not theorems: a planted defect fails them.

pinned.name: chess_lc_03
pinned.what: That the acceptance vectors carry the Chess Programming Wiki's perft counts for five reference positions, computed from FEN by the test itself, and that the counts are sums of isLegalMove over every move. prismpm verify replays them in the compiled guest.

pinned.name: Not claimed
pinned.what: That isLegalMove equals the rules of chess for every position: it is measured by perft, not proved. Draws by repetition, the fifty-move rule and insufficient material are not detected, because a request carries no game history.
